name: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Magnetar Lance ML-6 'Pulsar'
description:
An electromagnetic accelerator that fires a magnetically-charged penetrator which disrupts ferromagnetic materials along its flight path. The Pulsar's projectile generates an intense magnetic field that interferes with any iron-based material within 3 meters of its trajectory — pulling nails from walls, dragging weapons from hands, and destabilizing ferrofluid-based armor systems.

Zheng-Dao developed the ML-6 as an anti-armor weapon that defeats protective systems through magnetic disruption rather than kinetic penetration. The magnetically-charged penetrator warps and distorts ferrous armor plates as it approaches, creating gaps and weaknesses that the projectile then exploits. Against ferrofluid armor — an increasingly common defensive technology — the Pulsar's magnetic field draws the protective fluid away from the impact point, leaving the wearer exposed.

The weapon's magnetic effect extends beyond the target. Personnel near the flight path report magnetic interference with cybernetic implants containing ferrous components, and electronic systems within the disruption radius experience temporary malfunction.
legality: Licensed — military and corporate heavy weapons operators
specifications:
caliber: 8mm magnetically-charged tungsten-iron penetrator
effective_range: 50-800 meters
rate_of_fire: 1 round per 5 seconds
capacity: 4-round internal magazine
weight: 10.6 kg
power_source: Magnetic charge generator, integrated capacitor bank
tactical_use: The Pulsar is deployed against targets wearing ferrofluid armor or operating behind ferrous-material defenses. The weapon's magnetic disruption field extends its effective lethality beyond the direct impact point, affecting equipment and implants in a cone along the projectile's path. Operators use the ML-6 to 'clear a lane' of ferrous obstacles before kinetic engagement, and the weapon's disruptive effect on cybernetic implants makes it a psychological weapon against augmented combatants.
cultural_context: The Pulsar has created anxiety among populations with ferrous-component cybernetics — which includes most budget augmentations in the lower tiers. Expensive implants use non-ferrous materials, but affordable cybernetics often incorporate iron-based alloys. The ML-6 effectively discriminates between economic classes of augmentation, disrupting cheap implants while leaving expensive ones unaffected. This has led to accusations that the weapon was designed to disproportionately affect lower-tier populations.
story_hooks: A Pulsar round was fired through a crowd in the lower tiers. The magnetic disruption field caused cascade failures in budget cybernetics across dozens of bystanders — pacemakers stopped, prosthetic limbs locked, and ocular implants overloaded. The intended target was untouched by the magnetic effect because their augmentations were non-ferrous.

Zheng-Dao has developed a Pulsar variant that fires magnetically-charged rounds which remain magnetized after impact, creating a persistent disruption field at the point of impact. The potential for area denial against augmented populations has attracted both military interest and humanitarian condemnation.

physical_description.visual_profile: A bulky, purpose-built electromagnetic rifle with a pronounced angular aesthetic. The weapon has a distinctive boxy receiver with prominent capacitor housings along both sides. The barrel is oversized and slightly tapered, with visible cooling fins. Heavy, imposing, and deliberately industrial — designed to project raw technological force rather than elegance.
physical_description.dimensions: 127 cm overall length, 58 cm barrel, 12 cm width at receiver, 8 cm height at capacitor stack
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and substantial — 10.6 kg feels authoritative in the hands, requiring proper stance. Balanced toward the receiver due to the internal capacitor bank, with a slight front-heavy pull from the barrel assembly.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced carbon-composite frame with tungsten-alloy barrel shroud and steel reinforcement ribs. Capacitor housings are brushed aluminum.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal composite with brushed aluminum accents. The barrel shroud shows a dark gunmetal patina. Deliberate lack of gloss — designed for low-visibility ops.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with brushed aluminum silver on capacitor banks and barrel cooling fins. Accent copper trim on the charging port.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with aggressive checkering. Slight warmth to the touch due to capacitor proximity. The foregrip is wrapped in textured carbon-fiber tape.
distinctive_features: Twin cylindrical capacitor housings flanking the receiver, each with glowing charge-state indicator rings (soft blue when charged)
Visible electromagnetic focusing coil ring around the barrel muzzle
Magnetic charge meter — an analog gauge on the left side showing charge level via a needle
Four-round magazine well with oversized, fluted magazine release button
Vented heat sink fins along the barrel shroud
Weapon-mounted targeting crosshair reticle etched into the left receiver rail
Faint carbon scoring on the barrel shroud from sustained fire
Copper cooling vanes visible through semi-translucent panels on the capacitor housings
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries logo (stylized circular symbol with electromagnetic waves) stamped in matte chrome on the left receiver panel. Serial number and manufacturing date engraved on the barrel shroud. 'ML-6 PULSAR' designation in block letters on the right side of the receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained, though showing signs of regular use. The barrel shroud displays minor carbon scoring and thermal stress marks. The grip shows slight shine from operator perspiration. Capacitor housings are clean, indicating proper maintenance protocols. Not pristine — this is an active weapon, not a showpiece.
